doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Choosing Hamilton College and its cost
summary: He picked Hamilton after weekend visits; tuition was $400 a semester in the Depression.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What brought you to Hamilton? What about this place appealed to you?

Well when I was a senior in high school I narrowed down the places of opportunity to eight or nine and I sent for their material. And I picked three of them. My father sent me to each of them for a weekend. And the three were Oberlin, Middlebury and here. And I just came here, I felt wonderful, and we had some friends of my father’s who made me feel at home and so on and one guy over in the Theta Delta house was a buddy. So it felt natural that this is where I’d most like to be so I just came. I wasn’t looking for anything special, just a liberal arts education, but in those days a college education was a college education. You took what you could get. And I’ll say this for the record that — nobody would ever believe it — but the cost of coming to Hamilton College was $400 a semester. I ran across one of the old bills not too long ago. And my dad, this was of course in the middle of the depression, my dad paid $400 to send me to school. So think about that as you pay your daughter’s bills.
I’ll try to keep it in mind.
I just saw the minutes of the last trustee’s meeting, God it’s $32,000 to come to this school. Incredible.
